title: Think Like an Attacker
story: The guard dogs of Aata-gram only bark at strangers they have seen before. Real attackers are new. To defend, learn what they look for.
goal: Learn the one rule behind most attacks, then try the quick checks.

tests.label: Finish every try-it and quick check

hints: Read each block, then do the TRY IT and QUICK CHECK parts.
Every interactive block must be done to finish the lesson.
Take your time. Nothing here is timed.
socratic: Compare your result with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the most useful thing you learned here?

blocks.text:
Most security bugs come from one mistake: **trusting input**. Input can be a form field, a URL, a file name, an HTTP header or a command line argument.

If input reaches something powerful (a database, a shell, a file path, a web page) without being handled safely, an attacker can steer it.

blocks.title: Input steering a database
blocks.code:
name = input()
query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'"
print(query)

blocks.q: If a user types ' OR '1'='1 as the name, what happens to that query?
options: It matches every row, because the input became part of the SQL
blocks.why: The quote closes the string, and OR '1'='1 is always true. That is SQL injection.

blocks.q: What is the safe way to put user input into SQL?
options: Parameters (placeholders) so the database treats it only as data
blocks.why: Placeholders keep data and commands apart.

blocks.q: Which of these is NOT user input?
options: A constant string you wrote in your code
A file name from an upload
blocks.why: Constants written by you are trusted. Everything that arrives from outside is not.
